summary: This is a well-executed, fully preregistered confirmatory paired study comparing an LLM-only pipeline to a deterministic generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipeline on a 200-task synthetic NetOps intent→configuration bank. Execution and analysis artifacts appear complete and consistent with the preregistration; the archived manifest shows no technical failures and reproducible model/validator traces. The principal result is a null/negative confirmatory outcome: both conditions produced validator-passing configurations for all tasks (n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0), so the preregistered hypothesis of ≥50% relative reduction is not supported. The manuscript reports methods, preregistration, disclosure, and limitations. Several manuscript clarifications are required to remove remaining ambiguities about deterministic settings and emulator holdout details before finalisation.
critical_issues: Ambiguity about deterministic generation settings: the manuscript and preregistration state deterministic/shared-initial generation (temperature=0), but execution artifact model_configuration.json lists "temperature": null. This discrepancy must be explicitly resolved and supported by the archived provider-call traces (showing the actual temperature/seed or adapter-enforced determinism).
required_revisions: Clarify and correct the manuscript text to explicitly state the exact model-generation parameters used (temperature, seed/determinism mechanism, and any adapter-enforced settings). Provide an explicit pointer to the provider-call traces or model_configuration artifact (path + hash already present in the execution manifest) demonstrating the recorded setting so reviewers can verify determinism.

Report the Mininet emulator holdout selection and outcome in the Results (how many tasks were included in the emulator holdout, selection seed, and the explicit count of disagreements observed—if any). Cite the specific artifact(s) (path(s) and hash(es)) that contain the emulator traces or contamination_summary so the claim "no disagreements observed" is verifiable.

Add a concise, in-manuscript artifact summary (one short paragraph or a compact boxed list) giving the key reproducibility identifiers: preregistration SHA-256, execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256, execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA-256, and execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 (these hashes are present in the manifest and can be quoted in the five-page PDF). This makes the reproducibility claims easily verifiable by reviewers and readers without browsing the entire bundle.
optional_revisions: Briefly illustrate (1–2 representative examples) of tasks where the initial LLM output matched the reference to help readers understand why no repairs were applied (link to the corresponding execution/responses files).

Add a short sentence clarifying why the paired design used a shared initial candidate rather than independent condition generation and discuss methodological implications (this is permitted by the preregistration but worth emphasizing).

Include a succinct evidence-to-claim table and nearest-work comparison matrix as a supplemental figure or inline compact table (if space permits) to improve literature positioning and make the claim support easier to inspect.
